name: Cooked Quinoa (Intact Seed Coat & Saponin Warning)
whyItWorks: Quinoa is botanically a tiny seed, not a grain. When cooked, each seed unfurls a tiny fibrous tail and retains an indigestible seed coat. Thousands of tiny seeds pass largely intact into the bowel, causing mechanical irritation in strictures.
prepOrOrderInstructions: Stricture Warning: Avoid quinoa salads and bowls during active symptoms. Choose white rice, couscous, or peeled potatoes instead.
watchOuts: Tiny intact seeds pass undigested, irritating inflamed intestinal linings.
